title: Settings
upDesc: Each upstream is an independent PAT pool; a key bound to an upstream only uses that pool
upFormHint: Fill in the target upstream's own address and api_key; leave api_key empty for the same address to reuse the default upstream's key
upFieldUrlHint: Like http://127.0.0.1:8963 — no path, no trailing slash
upFieldKeyPlaceholder: Empty = no auth header (most upstreams don't need one)
upFieldKeyKeep: leave blank to keep the current key ({masked})
upDeleteDesc: Delete upstream “{name}”? Deletion is refused while keys or accounts are still bound to it — rebind or delete them first.
upNameUrlRequired: Name and upstream URL are both required
upHint: A key bound to an upstream only uses that upstream's PAT pool; unbound = default upstream (from the QC2API_BASE environment variable, not editable or deletable).
upEmptyDesc: Add an upstream to schedule requests by PAT pool groups
mapNewAliasDesc: Let downstream call a model by a familiar name, e.g. point `gpt-4o-mini` at `glm-5.2`. Setting the alias to `*` makes it the **fallback model**: every name that matches no mapping goes to it — note it also catches typoed model names, so those requests no longer fail with an explicit “model unavailable”.
mapEmptyDesc: Downstream can call models directly by the names in the upstream catalog
usersNewDesc: Administrators can add or remove accounts and change settings; read-only users can only look, which suits sharing status with colleagues.
roleUpdated: Role updated; the user's existing sessions are now invalid
resetPasswordDesc: All of this user's existing sessions will be revoked. At least 12 characters.
passwordRelogin: Your current session was revoked; sign in again with the new password
passwordOthersRevoked: All other sessions of that user were revoked
usersEmptyDesc: Keep at least one administrator account
deleteUserDesc: Once deleted, the user can no longer sign in. This cannot be undone.
tokensAdminRequiredDesc: Access tokens can call the admin API without signing in (including creating gateway keys and changing the account pool), so they are admin-only. Ask an administrator to change your role under Settings → Users.
tokensNewDesc: A long-lived credential for scripts / CI (qct_ prefix). It only authorizes the admin API, not model calls; the plaintext is shown once, on creation.
tokensCreatedDesc: Copy it now: the plaintext is shown only once.
tokensSessionOnlyHint: High-risk endpoints (updating, clearing logs, user management) still require a session login; tokens cannot call them.
tokensDeleteDesc: Scripts using this token stop working immediately (401). This cannot be undone.
tokensEmptyDesc: Create a token so scripts / CI can call the admin API without logging in
updAssetsPending: This release was just published and its archive is still uploading; updating now would return a 404. Try again in a few minutes or hit refresh.
updHint: Click “Start update” to update; accounts and settings are preserved automatically.
updCheckFailed: This check could not reach GitHub
updCheckFailedHint: Click “Check for updates” to try again. Unauthenticated GitHub access is rate-limited per hour; this happens when rate-limited.
updStaleNote: The results below are from {at} — do not rely on them to tell whether a new version exists.
updUpdatingHint: The service may restart briefly during the update (the page reconnects automatically) — do not shut down the server. Progress refreshes every 1.5 seconds.
updDoneRestart: The service restarted; refresh the page to confirm the version number.
updFailedDetail: Check the log below; accounts and configuration were not affected.
updOneClickDesc: Fetches the latest release from GitHub, replaces the code and frontend automatically and restarts the service. Accounts, keys, logs and settings are all preserved.
updConfirmDesc: The service is briefly interrupted during the update; it restarts automatically when done. Accounts and settings are unaffected.
updGhTitle: GitHub token (update checks and one-click updates)
updGhDesc: Unauthenticated GitHub access is limited to 60 requests per hour, and a shared egress (container/system proxy) can easily exhaust that, which shows up as a failed update check. With a token the quota is 5000/hour; read-only access to public-repo Releases is enough. Submitting empty clears the token.
updGhFromEnv: Currently using the environment variable injected at deployment (QC_GITHUB_TOKEN); what you fill in here has no effect.
updMirrorDesc: When direct GitHub access times out or release downloads stall, fill in the base URL of an acceleration service (e.g. `https://gh-proxy.com/`). Version checks and release downloads go through the mirror first and fall back to direct access on failure. The mirror forwards requests to a third party, so **the token above is not sent when the mirror is used**; **the mirror also takes part in fetching version info and checksums, which effectively makes it an update source — only use a service you trust.** Submitting empty restores direct access.
updMirrorCleared: Mirror cleared, back to direct connections
updMirrorActive: Active: {value} (falls back to direct when the download fails)
updMirrorFromEnv: Currently using the environment variable injected at deployment (QC_GITHUB_MIRROR): {value}
updMirrorNone: Not set: all requests go directly to GitHub.
updAutoDesc: When enabled, new versions are checked on an interval, and the one-click update runs **automatically** only inside the time window below (the panel restarts). Nothing happens if the check fails or release assets are not ready; after an auto-update failure for the same version, no retry for 24 hours.
updAutoWindowHint: The window uses the server's local time ({tz}); the same start and end means any time of day.
updAutoUnsupported: The current deployment does not support one-click updates, so automatic updates are unavailable; update manually per the repository docs.
updPkgDesc: For machines that cannot reach GitHub: download `qcoder-manager-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz` from the releases page, upload it here and update from it (**no network involved**). On upload it is verified to be a release package of this project and checked against the sha256 on the releases page.
updPkgShaPlaceholder: Paste the 64-character digest shown in the release notes
updPkgUploadedDesc: About {mb} MB — you can start the update now
updPkgNotCompared: this package has no release digest; the server will refuse to install it
updPkgCompareHint: Installing the package runs its code on this machine; fill in the checksum from the releases page to confirm it was not tampered with. In a truly offline environment where the checksum is unobtainable, set QC_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_PACKAGE=1 explicitly on the server.
updLogEmpty: No log yet. Progress appears here in real time once an update starts.
updLoadFailed: Update info is temporarily unavailable (the service may be restarting) — the current-version / new-version indicators are not reliable right now.
pgDesc:
Mirrors all business data on this machine (account notes, keys, request logs, usage statistics, settings…) to a PostgreSQL server. The panel keeps reading and writing the local database; PostgreSQL is only an **off-site safe**: if the server dies, install the panel on a new machine, fill in the same connection info, click “Restore from PostgreSQL” once, and the data comes back.

`.env` and the admin account file are not covered — bring those two yourself when restoring on a new machine.
pgHostHint: Hostname or IP of the PostgreSQL server. Private addresses are fine (e.g. 127.0.0.1, 172.17.0.1).
pgDbnameHint: Prefer a dedicated database: migration recreates tables with the same names, and existing tables of the same name will be replaced.
pgPasswordHint: Leave empty or keep the mask unchanged to keep the saved password. The password is stored in plaintext in the local database, protected only by file permissions (600).
pgSslmodeHint: libpq sslmode: prefer / require / disable, etc. Defaults to prefer (encrypt when possible).
pgAutoEnableDesc: When on, data is pushed to PostgreSQL automatically at the interval below.
pgIntervalHint: 0 means only manual pushes. 30–1440 is a sensible range.
pgKeepBackupDesc: Before restoring from PostgreSQL, save a copy of the current database under data/ so a mistaken restore can be undone.
pgAdminOnly: Only an admin session can change the settings or run a migration/restore.
pgExportDesc: Pushes all local data to PostgreSQL, replacing the old mirror there. Reads local data only; it is never modified.
pgExportConfirmDesc: The current local data will replace the old mirror on PostgreSQL. Local data is untouched, so you can push again at any time.
pgImportDesc: Replaces local data with the mirror on PostgreSQL. **This deletes all current local data** — use it only when moving to a new machine or recovering from data loss.
pgImportConfirmDesc: All local keys, logs, usage and settings will be replaced by the copy on PostgreSQL. If "Back up before restoring" is on, a copy is saved under data/ first.
pgNeedConfig: Fill in the host and database name and save before migrating or restoring.
pgWarn: **Restoring overwrites local data.** If all you want is "don't lose data", scheduled migration is enough; restore is only needed when changing machines or after real data loss.
pgLoadFailed: Backup configuration could not be loaded — this does not mean nothing was configured; please retry.
clUnavailableHint: The changelog ships with the release package (`CHANGELOG.md`). If you upgraded from an older version, run an update under System Update to fetch it; when running from source, make sure that file exists at the repository root.
clThisIsCurrent: This is the version you are running
clSeeAll: All versions: see the Releases page
clTruncated: Only the latest {n} of {total} versions are shown; see the repository Releases page for older ones.
aboutDesc: QCoder Manager provides the web console and public API gateway for the Qoder → OpenAI-compatible proxy: PAT account-pool onboarding, multi-upstream grouping, key distribution, IP control, request logs and usage statistics.
aboutUsage: Downstream setup: set the Base URL to `https://your-domain/v1` and use a `qk_...` key generated on the API keys page.
